findings.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — P1 confidence 75: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` builds the calendar updater with the requesting attendee's credentials rather than the booking organizer's credentials, so an attendee adding guests to another user's booking cannot update the organizer-owned calendar event.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — P2 confidence 100: `guests: z.array(z.string().email()),` accepts repeated new addresses that the dialog's separate uniqueness refinement rejects, and the handler forwards both copies through `data: guestsFullDetails`, violating the unique-guest input contract for direct API callers.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — P2 confidence 100: `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);` passes the original request instead of the filtered additions, so a request containing an existing attendee plus a new guest classifies the existing attendee as newly booked and sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of the guest-change notification.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:76 — Advisory P2 confidence 100: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` scans every existing attendee for each proposed guest, making growing bookings pay O(existing attendees × proposed guests) comparison work; the strongest rebuttal is that ordinary meetings are small, but neither collection is bounded here, and a precomputed email Set deletes the repeated linear membership scans while retaining the filter semantics.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:529 — P1 confidence 100: `emailsToSend.push(sendEmail(() => new OrganizerAddGuestsEmail({ calEvent: calendarEvent })));` and `...calendarEvent.attendees.map((attendee) => {` send host and attendee notifications even when the event metadata sets `disableStandardEmails.all.host` or `disableStandardEmails.all.attendee`, because the new helper neither accepts metadata nor applies the existing sibling notification guards.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:542 — Advisory P2 confidence 75: `return sendEmail(() => new AttendeeScheduledEmail(calendarEvent, attendee));` forwards `additionalNotes` unchanged when a caller supplies `hideCalendarNotes: true`, so recipients receive notes the scheduled-email path explicitly removes; the strongest rebuttal is that the current handler omits notes entirely, but the exported helper accepts CalendarEvent and its first caller that supplies the existing notes field bypasses that established flag contract.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — [P1 confidence=100] `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` runs after the attendee insert is committed, so a rejected calendar update leaves the new guests persisted without calendar updates or invitations and retrying the same guests fails the existing-attendee filter instead of completing the operation.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:170 — [P1 confidence=100] `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails");` swallows notification failures before returning success, so a rejected invitation send leaves guests uninformed while the caller sees "Guests added" and retrying their already-persisted addresses cannot resend the invitations.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — [P2 confidence=100] `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` silently removes blocked addresses from a mixed valid-and-blocked request while the handler returns `return { message: "Guests added" };`, so the organizer receives success without being told that requested guests were not added.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — [P2 confidence=75] `guests: z.array(z.string().email()),` accepts uncapped guest batches that are persisted and expanded into parallel invitation sends and the organizer template's `replyTo: [this.calEvent.organizer.email, ...this.calEvent.attendees.map(({ email }) => email)],`, so sufficiently large batches or repeated additions exhaust request resources and exceed mail-provider recipient/header limits without a booking-level bound.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — P1 confidence 100: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` compares unnormalized input against lowercased blacklist entries, so submitting `blocked@EXAMPLE.COM` bypasses a `blocked@example.com` blacklist entry and adds the prohibited recipient to the booking and notification delivery.

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — P1 confidence 75: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` builds the calendar updater with the requesting attendee's credentials rather than the booking organizer's credentials, so an attendee adding guests to another user's booking cannot update the organizer-owned calendar event.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` gets the credentials of the requesting user (who could be an attendee), not the booking organizer. The code at line 158 shows `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` where `ctx.user` is the authenticated user making the request. The permission check at lines 47-52 allows attendees to add guests (`isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find(...)`), but the EventManager is then initialized with the attendee's credentials rather than the organizer's credentials. This means when an attendee adds guests, the calendar update would fail or use wrong credentials since the attendee doesn't own the organizer's calendar event.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — [P1 confidence=100] `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` runs after the attendee insert is committed, so a rejected calendar update leaves the new guests persisted without calendar updates or invitations and retrying the same guests fails the existing-attendee filter instead of completing the operation.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a transactional consistency issue in addGuests.handler.ts. Looking at the diff, the handler first commits attendees to the database via `prisma.booking.update` (lines 85-99), then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` (line 165). If the calendar update fails, the attendees are already persisted in the database. The uniqueGuests filter (lines 68-72) checks against existing `booking.attendees`, so retrying with the same guests would filter them out as duplicates, preventing completion of the calendar update. This is a real atomicity/consistency bug where partial failure leaves the system in an inconsistent state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:170 — [P1 confidence=100] `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails");` swallows notification failures before returning success, so a rejected invitation send leaves guests uninformed while the caller sees "Guests added" and retrying their already-persisted addresses cannot resend the invitations.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at lines 168-172 in addGuests.handler.ts that email sending failures are caught and only logged with console.log, then the function returns success with 'Guests added' message. This means: 1) Guests are persisted to the database (line 85-99), 2) If sendAddGuestsEmails fails, the error is swallowed, 3) The caller receives success response, 4) Guests won't receive invitation emails but are already in the database. This is a real bug - silent failure of a critical notification with no way to retry since the guests are already persisted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — [P2 confidence=100] `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` silently removes blocked addresses from a mixed valid-and-blocked request while the handler returns `return { message: "Guests added" };`, so the organizer receives success without being told that requested guests were not added.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that when some guests are blacklisted, they are silently filtered out by the `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` check on line 77. The handler then proceeds to add only the non-blacklisted guests and returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` without any indication that some requested guests were not added. This is a real usability/correctness issue where the user gets a success message but some of their requested guests were silently dropped.

Without any cap, a malicious user could add thousands of guests, causing database bloat, email sending resource exhaustion, and potentially exceeding mail provider limits. This is a real security/resource exhaustion vulnerability introduced by the new code.
